transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I'm just so distressed about how awful my skin looks, especially with all the terrible acne and scars on my face. It feels like it's all I can think about, even though everyone else keeps telling me they can't really see anything. It's just incredibly overwhelming and I don't know what to do.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time doing certain things because of this concern, like checking your skin in the mirror, picking at it, or trying to hide or cover it up?

Yes, I spend hours every day doing those things. I constantly check the mirror and pick at any tiny bump to try to fix it, which usually just makes it look worse. Then I have to spend a really long time trying to hide everything with heavy makeup before I can even leave the house.
Aside from your skin and appearance, do you experience other repetitive thoughts or behaviors, such as a need to wash your hands constantly, check locks, or keep things in a perfect order?

No, I don't experience anything like that. I don't feel any need to constantly wash my hands, check locks, or keep objects in a perfect order. My worries and behaviors are really just focused on my skin and how I look.
How certain are you that your skin actually looks as terrible as you see it? Do you think it's possible that your mind might be making these flaws seem much worse than they really are?

I am absolutely certain that my skin looks as terrible as I see it. Even if other people say they don't notice much, the acne and scars are incredibly obvious to me and completely ruin my appearance. It's just so hard to believe this is all in my mind when the flaws feel so real and visible.
Do you believe there is an underlying medical illness, infection, or parasite causing these skin issues, or do you view this purely as an issue with your physical appearance?

I view this purely as an issue with my physical appearance, and I don't think there is any underlying infection or parasite. I am just extremely preoccupied with what I see as terrible flaws, scars, and acne on my face. That's why I end up picking at my skin so much to try and 'fix' it.
Do you ever feel like people are staring at you, talking about you, or judging you because of your skin, or do you have any other concerns that people are spying on you or trying to harm you?

Yes, I constantly feel like people are staring at my face and judging me because of how awful my skin looks. But I don't have any thoughts that people are spying on me or trying to harm me; it's really just about my appearance.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were ['Body Dysmorphic Disorder', 'Delusional Disorder']. The patient's presentation is characterized by a severe preoccupation with perceived flaws in physical appearance (skin, acne, scars) that are unobservable or appear slight to others, accompanied by repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, skin picking, heavy makeup) and significant distress. Although the patient has delusional-level conviction regarding these flaws, this is classified under Body Dysmorphic Disorder (with absent insight/delusional beliefs) rather than Delusional Disorder, Somatic Type, because the focus is specifically on physical appearance defects. Therefore, the diagnosis is Body Dysmorphic Disorder.
